title: Wanderburg Difficulty: What We Know So Far (2026)
description: Wanderburg difficulty: what official sources confirm about settings, scaling, and harder modes. Details are thin right now, so no numbers are invented here.
h1: Wanderburg Difficulty: What's Known So Far

sections.h2: Is There a Difficulty Setting in Wanderburg?
paragraphs: Right now, no difficulty selector or named difficulty tiers are publicly documented for Wanderburg. Store pages and the official site list the game's core features — captains, weapons, runs, and builds — but we could not confirm a separate difficulty option.
If you are looking for a concrete answer, treat it as 待确认: the sources are thin, and nothing should be reported as a confirmed mode yet.

sections.h2: How Difficulty Is Likely to Work
paragraphs: Wanderburg's run-based structure (captains, weapons, combos) means challenge is probably tied to progression and per-run variance rather than a fixed menu setting. Enemy scaling, unlock tiers, or optional self-imposed restrictions would all be typical for this kind of game — but none of this is officially confirmed.

For now, the gameplay page covers the systems that are documented, and the builds page shows which loadouts players are testing. Difficulty-specific numbers, hazards, or modifiers are not published anywhere we can verify.

sections.h2: Where to Watch for Confirmed Difficulty Info
paragraphs: The most reliable places to check are the official Wanderburg Discord announcements, the Steam store page notes, and the roadmap. Any announcement about difficulty options would likely appear there — and on this wiki's updates and roadmap pages — before anywhere else.
Until then, the free demo is the practical way to judge how challenging the game feels. If difficulty systems get confirmed, this page will be updated with sourced details only.

note: No difficulty modes, scaling rules, or modifiers are confirmed by official sources yet — treat all specifics as 待确认.
